items.readable_text:
Content:
The inverse Laplace transform of a function [MATH: F(s)] is denoted [MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1} \left\{ F(s) \right\}.]

Content:
To find the inverse Laplace transform, we first find the function [MATH: f(t)] whose Laplace transform is [MATH: F(s)\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: F(s) = \mathcal{L} \left\{ f(t) \right\}]

Content:
Then, we have

Content:
[MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1} \left\{ F(s) \right\} = \mathcal{L}^{-1} \left\{ \mathcal{L} \left\{ f(t) \right\} \right\} = f(t).]

Content:
Note that the addition and scalar multiplication properties also hold for the inverse Laplace transform:

Content:
- The addition property:
[MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{F(s) + G(s) \right\} = \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ F(s) \right\} + \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ G(s) \right\}]
- The scalar multiplication property:
[MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ c \cdot F(s) \right\} = c \cdot \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ F(s) \right\}]

Content:
Next, we will look at an example of calculating an inverse Laplace transform.

sections.normalized_html: Find [MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{F(s)\right\}] for [MATH: F(s)=\dfrac{4e^{-s}-2}{s}.]
sections.readable_text: Find [MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{F(s)\right\}] for [MATH: F(s)=\dfrac{4e^{-s}-2}{s}.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we decompose the fraction into a sum of partial fractions:

[MATH: \dfrac{4e^{-s}-2}{s} =\dfrac{4e^{-s}}{s} - \dfrac{2}{s}]

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have [MATH: L{u_{1}(t)}|= (e^{− s})/(s), s > 0,; L{1}|= (1)/(s), s > 0,] where [MATH: u_1(t)=u(t-1)] is the unit step function.

Therefore, using the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get [MATH: L^{− 1}{(4e^{− s})/(s) − (2)/(s)}|= 4L^{− 1}{(e^{− s})/(s)} − 2L^{− 1}{(1)/(s)}; = 4u_{1}(t) − 2.]

So the inverse Laplace transform of [MATH: F(s)=\dfrac{4e^{-s}-2}{s}] is [MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{F(s)\right\} = f(t)= 4 u_1(t) - 2.]

First, we write [MATH: F(s)] as a sum of partial fractions:

[MATH: \dfrac{3s}{(s-4)(s+2)} = \dfrac{2}{s-4} + \dfrac{1}{s+2}]

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have [MATH: L{e^{4t}}|= (1)/(s − 4), s > 4,; L{e^{− 2t}}|= (1)/(s + 2), s > − 2.]

So the inverse Laplace transform of [MATH: F(s)=\dfrac{3s}{(s-4)(s+2)}] is [MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ F(s) \right\} = f(t)=2e^{4t} + e^{-2t}.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The inverse Laplace transform of a function [MATH: F(s)] is denoted [MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1} \left\{ F(s) \right\}.]

Content:
To find the inverse Laplace transform, we first find the function [MATH: f(t)] whose Laplace transform is [MATH: F(s)\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: F(s) = \mathcal{L} \left\{ f(t) \right\}]

Content:
Then, we have

Content:
[MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1} \left\{ F(s) \right\} = \mathcal{L}^{-1} \left\{ \mathcal{L} \left\{ f(t) \right\} \right\} = f(t).]

Content:
Note that the addition and scalar multiplication properties also hold for the inverse Laplace transform:

Content:
- The addition property:
[MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{F(s) + G(s) \right\} = \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ F(s) \right\} + \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ G(s) \right\}]
- The scalar multiplication property:
[MATH: \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ c \cdot F(s) \right\} = c \cdot \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ F(s) \right\}]

Content:
Next, we will look at an example of calculating an inverse Laplace transform.
